chunks: 3287 - Al-Hasan ibn Zayd narrated something similar to what he mentioned from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, who said:

“ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb was brought Qudāmah ibn Maẓʿūn, who had drunk wine. Two men testified against him: one of them was a eunuch, and he was ʿAmr al-Tamīmī, and the other was al-Muʿallā ibn al-Jārūd. One of them testified that he saw him drinking, and the other testified that he saw him vomiting wine. So ʿUmar sent for some of the companions of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, among whom was ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام. He said to ʿAlī عليه السلام, ‘What do you say, O Abū al-Ḥasan? For you are the one about whom the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “The most knowledgeable of this Ummah and the most judicial of it in truth.” These two have differed in their testimony.’ So ʿAlī عليه السلام said, ‘They have not differed in their testimony, and he would not have vomited it until he had drunk it.’ He said, ‘Is the testimony of a eunuch admissible?’ He عليه السلام said, ‘The loss of his testicles is nothing but like the loss of some of his limbs.’”

key_terms.أَعْلَمُ: most knowledgeable; used in praise of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام
key_terms.أَقْضَاهَا: the one most capable of judging; referring to judicial correctness in truth
key_terms.الْخَمْرَ: wine or intoxicant, the substance involved in the offense
key_terms.تَجُوزُ: is valid or admissible in legal judgment
key_terms.خَصِيٌّ: a eunuch; here, a witness whose legal admissibility is discussed
key_terms.شَهَادَتِهِمَا: their testimony; the paired witness statements under examination
key_terms.شَهِدَ: gave testimony or bore witness in a legal setting

ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of a eunuch accepted in Islamic legal rulings, and how are differing witness statements reconciled?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts a legal case in which Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام clarifies that two apparently different testimonies are in fact corroborative, since vomiting wine indicates prior drinking. It also states that being a eunuch does not invalidate a person's testimony, establishing a juridical principle regarding admissible witnesses.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3287 - And Al-Hasan bin Zayd narrated something similar from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as), from his father, Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), who said:

"Umar bin Al-Khattab was presented with Qudamah bin Maz'un, who had drunk alcohol. Two men testified against him-one of them was a eunuch, Amr Al-Tamimi, and the other was Al-Mu'alla bin Al-Jarood. One of them testified that he saw him drinking, and the other testified that he saw him vomiting alcohol. Umar then sent for a group of the companions of the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, among them Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as).
Umar said to Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as): 'What do you say, O Abu Al-Hasan? For you are the one about whom the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, said: "The most knowledgeable of this nation and the one who judges with truth."'
Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said: 'They have not differed in their testimony, for he would not have vomited it unless he had drunk it.'
Umar then asked: 'Is the testimony of a eunuch acceptable?'
Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) replied: 'The loss of his testicles is no different than the loss of some other part of his body.'"
